request: Analyze GSE256152 for PMID 38576560 (Transcriptomics and metabonomics study on the effect of exercise combined with curcumin supplementation on breast cancer in mice.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Illumina PE), 4T1-luc orthotopic breast tumour tissue, BALB/c mice; HISAT2 to GRCm39, HTSeq read counts, FPKM for display
final.sample_inclusion: 3 tumours per tumour group sequenced (S2.3.p1); 12 samples total (S3.2.p1); CK (no tumour) group not sequenced
final.primary_estimand: Effect of daily swimming exercise on breast-tumour gene expression: Tnm_swim vs Tnm (both vehicle gavage); secondary: combination (curcumin + swimming) vs Tnm
planned_contrasts: Tnm_swim vs Tnm (S3.2.p3; paper: 134 DEGs, 79 up / 55 down)
Tnm_union vs Tnm (S3.2.p3; paper: 445 DEGs, 154 up / 291 down)
Tnm_cur vs Tnm (S3.2.p3; paper: 107 DEGs, 28 up / 79 down; non-exercise contrast)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; one tumour per independent mouse
final.normalization: DESeq2 size factors on HTSeq read counts (S2.3.p1; GEO data_processing)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 pairwise vs Tnm (S2.3.p1); GEO data_processing says DESeq 1.30.0
final.paper_results: S3.2.p3 counts above; S3.2.p4 union-vs-Tnm KEGG: calcium, Wnt, IL-17 signalling with CAMK1G, WNT5A, IL6

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.1.p2 defines four tumour groups (2x2 of swimming x curcumin gavage). S2.3.p1: three tumours per group sequenced, DESeq2, |log2FC| > 1 and P < 0.05 (raw p-value). S3.2.p3 reports DEG counts for cur/swim/union each vs Tnm. The exercise question is Tnm_swim vs Tnm (single factor exercise, both vehicle); union vs Tnm is the combined intervention.

checks: GEO extract_protocol describes Tnm/Tnm+swim/Tnm+cur/Tnm+union groups as in S2.1.p2
12 GEO samples = 4 groups x 3, matching S2.3.p1 and S3.2.p1
matrix columns Tnm1-3, Tnm_swim1-3, Tnm_cur1-3, Tnm_union1-3 match GEO titles

ownership.reasoning: Data availability statement (S7.p1) deposits RNA-seq as GSE256152; the deposited Gene_exp_with_symbol file is the only supplementary matrix and its sample names equal the paper's group names.

alignment.reasoning: prep/extract_read_counts.py keeps the 12 ':read count' columns and renames them by name to the GEO titles (Tnm_swim1 -> Tnm-swim-1, Tnm_union1 -> Tnm+union-1, ...); alignment is then exact on metadata 'title'. grp is extracted from the title prefix. Note: GEO treatment field labels swim samples 'corn oil' (vehicle), consistent with S2.1.p2 where Tnm and Tnm_swim get vehicle gavage.

matrix.reasoning: The deposited file has paired ':read count' and ':fpkm' columns per sample; the read-count columns are all integers with no missing values (checked in prep script). GEO data_processing: HTSeq 0.9.1 read counts, FPKM only for normalization display. Paper input to DESeq2 is the read counts (S2.3.p1).

candidates.reason_rejected: linear-normalized; DESeq2 needs counts and the paper used counts

design.reasoning: One control (Tnm) with three treated levels (S3.2.p3 compares each vs Tnm). Exercise effect = swim vs Tnm (primary). Union vs Tnm is the paper's combined-treatment contrast (exercise + curcumin, not an isolated exercise effect). Cur vs Tnm is reported by the paper but is not an exercise contrast; run to compare counts. Union vs cur (exercise effect on a curcumin background) is not in the paper -> exploratory. n=3 per group.

candidates.reason_rejected: paper does not test main effects or interaction; it compares each group to Tnm
encodes only curcumin vs corn oil; exercise is only in the title

covariance.reasoning: Independent mice, one tumour each, randomized to groups (S2.1.p2). No batch, sex (all female BALB/c implied) or lane field recorded in GEO.

deviations: pydeseq2 instead of R DESeq2; GEO data_processing names DESeq 1.30.0 while paper says DESeq2
Paper's two-group comparisons are run as two-group subsets (only the two groups' samples), as in a standard pairwise DESeq2 pipeline; the exploratory union vs cur also as a subset

method.reasoning: Raw HTSeq counts support DESeq2, which the paper used (S2.3.p1). Each paper contrast is fit on the two groups' samples only, the typical vendor pipeline behaviour; a joint 4-group model is run as sensitivity for the primary exercise contrast.

threshold.reasoning: S2.3.p1: |log2FoldChange| > 1 and P-value < 0.05 (raw p, as also stated in GEO data_processing). Audit: BH padj < 0.05, no fold-change rule.

caveats: n = 3 tumours per group; raw-p threshold without multiple-testing correction, so DEG lists include many expected false positives
Union vs Tnm reflects curcumin + exercise combined, not exercise alone
pydeseq2 vs R DESeq2/DESeq 1.30.0 can change raw-p DEG counts

Direction balance contradicts the paper: swim vs Tnm ours 73 up / 138 down vs paper 79 up / 55 down; cur vs Tnm ours 110 up / 54 down vs paper 28 up / 79 down; union vs Tnm ours 286 up / 237 down vs paper 154 up / 291 down. Sign convention here is treatment over Tnm; the paper's convention is not stated, and no single sign flip reconciles all three contrasts
Paper's union-vs-Tnm KEGG pathways: IL-17 signalling reproduced by ORA (adj p 0.031); Wnt (raw p 0.06) and calcium signalling (raw p 0.12) not significant in our ORA

study.reasoning: S3.2.p3 counts; S3.2.p4 / Fig. 3C genes in the combination-vs-Tnm enriched pathways.

discrepancies.data: GEO extract protocol: 5 per group; 3 tumours per group sequenced either way
GEO protocol text mentions mm9 in one field and GRCm39 assembly in another

executions.reasoning: Paper's curcumin contrast (non-exercise), for count comparison

enrichment.reasoning: Paper ran GO/KEGG on each contrast's DEGs (S3.2.p4, Figs. S1-S2)
Paper's KEGG result (calcium, Wnt, IL-17) for the combination (S3.2.p4)
